transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, um… thanks for seeing me. I guess I’m here because I’ve been feeling like I’ve really messed things up. I fell behind at work, and the apartment situation got away from me, and I can’t stop thinking that I’ve ruined things for everyone.

I know that probably sounds dramatic… I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is. It’s just this feeling that I deserve whatever bad thing happens next, and I haven’t been able to shake it.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um… it’s been a while, I guess. Not forever, but… about a year and two months, maybe. It really seemed to start after that pipe burst and I had to move into the smaller apartment. My routines kind of fell apart after that. I don’t know if that’s the kind of timeline you mean.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things the way you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once liked?

Yeah… I mean, not completely, I guess, but most days I wake up with this kind of flat, heavy sadness. Things that used to help me feel like myself—putting on a record, cooking something, messing around with electronics—just don’t really… reach me the same way anymore. I still try sometimes, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve given up or anything. It’s just not like it used to be.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, have you felt restless or fidgety more than before?

A little slower, I think. Not dramatically, I don’t think anyone’s complained or anything… but at work I’ll catch myself with my hands just kind of hovering over the keyboard, and it takes me longer than it should to answer simple support tickets.

It’s like my brain and my body are on a delayed connection sometimes, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself feeling more guilty or worthless than usual, even about things that wouldn’t have bothered you much before?

Yeah… I guess I do. I mean, I know everybody gets behind sometimes, so I don’t want to make it sound overly dramatic, but… I keep feeling like I’ve messed things up for everyone.

At work, falling behind makes me feel like I’m causing problems for other people. And with the apartment situation, I keep thinking I should’ve handled it better, like I lost control of it somehow. It turns into this feeling that I’ve ruined things and… that maybe I deserve whatever bad thing happens next. I know that probably sounds harsh. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that you feel more tired or that you have less energy than you used to, even when you’re not doing much?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I do feel worn down some days, but I don’t know if it’s more than what anyone would feel, you know? I can still get through what I need to do most of the time.

Maybe my energy isn’t great, but I haven’t really been tracking it. Is that… is that what you’re asking?
Have you ever felt so low or hopeless that you’ve thought about hurting yourself or that life isn’t worth living?

I… I don’t have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I don’t want to scare anyone.

But, yeah… sometimes when it gets really low, I catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. Like then nobody would have to deal with me anymore. I know that sounds bad, I’m sorry. I haven’t made any plan, though.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over the past year?

Not really, I don’t think so. My appetite maybe goes up and down a little like anyone’s, but I haven’t noticed a big change or anything that seemed significant.

And weight-wise… I don’t think there’s been anything major. I guess I haven’t been watching it closely, but nothing that stood out to me. Is that okay?
Have you ever felt this way before, like you were stuck in a low mood for a long time, or is this the first time you’ve experienced something like this?

I think… this is the first time it’s lasted like this. I mean, I’ve had bad stretches before, like anyone, but this has been going on for about a year and two months.

It really started after that pipe burst and I had to move into the smaller apartment. My routines kind of fell apart after that, and I guess I just never got back to feeling like myself. I don’t know if that’s the kind of timeline you mean.
Have you ever had a period of time before this one where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve had rough weeks before, or times where I was stressed and didn’t feel like doing much, but I don’t remember anything lasting more than two weeks like this.

At least not in a way that felt… like something was really wrong, if that makes sense. Is that helpful?
Have you ever had any other periods in your life, before this one, where your mood was low and you lost interest in things for more than a couple of weeks?

I don’t think so… I know you asked something similar, and I’m trying to be accurate. I’ve had stressful times, sure, but I can’t really point to another period before this where I was low and not interested in things for more than a couple weeks.

At least nothing that I would’ve thought of that way at the time. Does that answer it okay?
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt unusually high, extremely energized, or overly confident, even for a short while?

No, I don’t think so. I’ve had times where I was maybe a little more productive or in a better mood, but not unusually high or overly confident like that.

I don’t think anyone would’ve described me that way either. Does that answer what you mean?
Before this current period, have you ever had an episode where your mood was so low that it felt like a major depression, even if it didn’t last this long?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve had times where I was sad or kind of worn down, but I wouldn’t say it felt like a major depression before this.

I’m trying not to overstate it. Nothing really stands out to me from before as an episode like that.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when your mood was so low that it felt like a major depression, even if it didn’t last as long as this one?

I don’t think so… I know it sounds like the same answer, but before this, I can’t really think of a time that felt like that.

I’ve had normal bad stretches, I guess, but not something I would’ve called a major depression. I hope that’s clear enough.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than a week or two, even if it didn’t last as long as this one?

I don’t think so, not for more than a week or two. I mean, I’ve had rough days or maybe a few days where I didn’t feel like doing much, but I don’t remember it lasting like that before this.

I’m sorry if I’m not giving you much there—I just don’t want to make it sound worse than it was.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when your mood was so low that it felt like a major depression, even if it didn’t last as long as this one?

I don’t think I have, no. I mean, I’ve definitely had periods where I was stressed or down, like anyone, but nothing before this that I would’ve thought of as a major depression.

I hope that answers it okay—I’m not trying to dodge the question, I just don’t remember anything like that before.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when your mood was so low that it met the criteria for a major depressive episode, even if it was shorter in duration?

I don’t think so… not that I can identify. Before this, I had times where I was unhappy or stressed, but I wouldn’t say it met that kind of level.

I’m sorry, I know you’ve asked it a few ways—I just don’t want to overstate it. I really can’t think of a time before this that fits.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks, even if it didn’t feel as severe as this one?

No, I don’t think so. I’ve had bad stretches before, sure, but not where it went on more than two weeks with feeling down or not enjoying things like that.

I hope that’s clear—I’m trying to be accurate and not make it sound like I had something before that I really didn’t.
